items.followUp: What happens to the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction when all enzyme active sites are occupied?

rubric.why: Saturation means substrate occupies the enzyme’s available active sites.
rubric.description: States that substrate molecules occupy all available enzyme active sites.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the occupation of the enzyme active sites by substrate.

rubric.why: At saturation, the enzymes are working at their maximum rate and extra substrate cannot raise the rate further.
rubric.description: States the consequence of saturation for the reaction rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate is maximal or cannot increase further.

modelAnswer: Saturation of active sites occurs when substrate molecules occupy all the available active sites of the enzymes.
The reaction reaches its maximum rate, and adding extra substrate cannot increase it.

items.followUp: Explain the three main stages of the Calvin cycle and show how carbon dioxide is used to make carbohydrate.

rubric.why: Identifies the dark reaction as light-independent or gives its location in the chloroplast.
rubric.description: Defines the dark reaction or states where it occurs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the light-independent stage or locating it in the stroma.

rubric.why: Carbon fixation combines carbon dioxide with RuBP to form PGA.
rubric.description: Describes carbon fixation and its products.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing carbon dioxide and RuBP forming PGA.

rubric.why: PGA is reduced to PGAL using energy and reducing power from the light reaction.
rubric.description: Describes the reduction of PGA to PGAL.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the conversion of PGA to PGAL, with ATP and NADPH or reduction.

rubric.why: Some PGAL leaves the cycle and is used to make carbohydrate.
rubric.description: States the use of some PGAL to form glucose or another carbohydrate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the carbohydrate product made from PGAL.

rubric.why: Regeneration of RuBP completes the cycle and allows carbon fixation to continue.
rubric.description: Shows that remaining PGAL regenerates RuBP and completes the cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing regeneration of RuBP in the cycle.

modelAnswer: The dark reaction is the light-independent stage of photosynthesis and occurs in the chloroplast stroma.
Carbon fixation: carbon dioxide combines with the five-carbon acceptor RuBP to form PGA.
Reduction: ATP and NADPH are used to convert PGA into PGAL.
Some PGAL leaves the cycle and is used to make glucose; the remaining PGAL regenerates RuBP.
Cycle: carbon dioxide + RuBP → PGA → PGAL → glucose (some PGAL); remaining PGAL → RuBP → cycle continues.
